newsitem.title: USA: IMF mission starts Ukraine talks next week.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission starts Ukraine talks next week.

text.p: A monitoring mission from the International Monetary Fund arrives in Ukraine this weekend for talks on a long-delayed credit of up to $3 billion, an IMF official said on Wednesday.
The talks, expected to last about two weeks, will start at the beginning of next week, the official said.
Long delays in approving Ukraine's 1997 budget has prevented agreement on releasing the IMF funds, designed to speed the transition to a capitalist-style market economy in the former Soviet republic.

But the IMF team is bound to take comfort from a parliamentary decision on Tuesday to approve the key expenditure and revenue figures in the budget, which should have been passed at the start of the year.
The document envisages revenues of 22.39 billion hryvnias ($12.1 billion) and expenditure of 28.12 billion hryvnias.

Parliament also rejected a government proposal that said Treasury Bills would be the only domestic deficit funding mechanism, but Central Bank chairman Viktor Yushchenko told reporters in Kiev on Wednesday that the central bank would not issue inflationary credits.

"The firm position of the National Bank of Ukraine, in agreement with the Ministry of Finance is that 1997 will be the first year the country will not issue credits to cover the budget deficit," he said.
The Group of Seven industrialized nations criticized Ukraine at their weekend summit in Denver, urging Kiev to step up economic reforms and make life easier for investors.

It was the second time in two months that the G7 had urged Kiev to implement its ambitious reform package. Finance Ministers and central bank chiefs said in April that they were growing increasingly worried and reforms were needed soon.
